papers.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds

summary.tldr: BrickWright is a framework using the BrickLayer Python API and physical validity feedback to enable AI coding agents to achieve a 100% physical validity rate when generating LEGO builds from text or image prompts.
key_points: BrickLayer API reduces inference costs by 50% compared to raw LDraw code by providing an ergonomic assembly API and an automated physical feasibility validator.
Physical feasibility is defined as using real parts, eliminating floating or colliding parts, and maintaining structural connectivity where possible.
BrickWright increases physical validity rates from baseline levels (9% for GPT-6 Luna, 69% for GPT-6 Astra) to 100% across a test set of 512 prompts.
The framework improves prompt adherence for lightweight models, maintains it for stronger agents, and outperforms domain-specialized models on text-to-brick tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables pre-trained LLM agents to reliably generate 3D models that can actually be assembled in the real world without requiring dedicated, task-specific model fine-tuning.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages

summary.tldr: Analysis of two diffusion language models reveals that inference cost per token varies significantly by task, language tokenization density, and answer correctness, rather than remaining constant.
key_points: DiffusionGemma requires over three times as many forward passes per token for open-ended story writing compared to input-heavy tasks like grammar correction.
Per-token generation cost increases when outputs contain novel text relative to the input, rely on task-rare words, or involve highly tokenized multilingual scripts.
Within reasoning traces, final answers that repeat prior chain-of-thought steps are computationally cheap, whereas introducing new content increases required forward passes.

Incorrect solutions to math problems require more passes per token than correct ones, enabling a decoding-speed candidate weighting method that outperforms majority voting by up to 4.2 points without extra compute.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding task-dependent computation in diffusion language models allows developers to predict inference costs more accurately and leverage decoding speed as a signal to improve model accuracy.

papers.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments

summary.tldr: TARSphere is a full-stack framework featuring a physics simulator with NPCs, an event-driven state machine, an MLLM-driven brain harness, and a 360-episode benchmark for long-horizon embodied agents in dynamic environments.
key_points: TARSphere-Infra executes robot policies in a physics simulator using an event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) to track state and evaluate task outcomes via completed actions and dialogue.
TARSphere-Harness uses frozen multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to control multi-level executable skills based on observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback.

TARSphere-Bench consists of 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes with 5 paired test conditions evaluating perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task updates, human coordination, and intent understanding.

Benchmarking of 8 MLLMs showed general-purpose models outperforming specialized embodied models, while highlighting persistent failure modes in handling task updates, human interactions, and execution safety (collisions and falls).
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a unified platform for testing and improving the physical safety, adaptability, and social coordination of language-model-driven robots in changing real-world environments.

papers.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research

summary.tldr: SplatLab is an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reproduces baselines, generates and trains plugin extensions, runs ablations, and writes fully traceably backed manuscripts.
key_points: Uses a verified-reproduction backbone and a seven-category 3DGS taxonomy wrapping EVOLVE-BLOCK markers to mutate plugin candidates.
Evaluates candidates using a cascade-weighted Elo tournament across eight islands based on measured GPU PSNR, incorporating verbal-gradient feedback and a standing falsifier.
Enforces strict traceability by binding every reported manuscript number to logged training runs, preventing run termination if any claim lacks backing.
Achieved PSNR gains of +0.18 to +3.78 dB over reproduced targets across Mip-NeRF 360, LLFF, and novel astrophotographic nebula rendering.
summary.why_it_matters: It compresses the months-long manual cycle of reproducing, extending, and documenting 3D Gaussian Splatting research into days of mostly autonomous compute.

papers.title: SEAM: Spectral Embedding Alignment and Merging for Low-Resource TTS

summary.tldr: SEAM is a zero-audio vocabulary expansion method for conditional TTS that constructs new token embeddings using spectral filtering and closed-form ridge regression alignment.
key_points: Constructs target token embeddings directly from existing subtokens without requiring paired audio data.
Applies a spectral filter to subtokens to preserve temporal phonetic order, overcoming limitations of structure-agnostic pooling.
Uses closed-form ridge regression to align newly constructed embeddings with the model's pretrained conditioning manifold.
Reduces sample complexity by 75% compared to random initialization and mean pooling, requiring up to 4x less training data across three languages and two TTS architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient cross-lingual and low-resource adaptation of speech synthesis models by drastically reducing the audio data required to expand model vocabularies.

papers.title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding

summary.tldr: RIPPLE is a recovery-oriented training framework that bridges the critique-to-action handoff gap in long-horizon agentic coding by internalizing process-level teacher guidance into a single self-recovering policy.
key_points: Addresses the Critique-to-Action Handoff Gap, where coding agents generate correct critiques but fail to adjust their execution trajectory.
Uses a prefix-only teacher to supply evidence-grounded recovery supervision without relying on future actions or terminal outcomes.
Applies reinforcement learning with stage-specific credit assignment for reflection triggering, diagnosis, and corrective action, using local validity signals to gate trajectory advantages.
Eliminates the need for an auxiliary critic at deployment while achieving an arithmetic mean improvement of 4.8 score points across four repository-level benchmarks.
Shows recovery performance gains depend on prefix diagnostic evidence and repository state reversibility within budget constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM coding agents to autonomously self-correct complex execution errors at inference time without relying on external critic models or future-looking supervision during training.

papers.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy

summary.tldr: A novel implementation of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy fixes two numerical bugs—Softmax Collapse and Softmax Cancellation—improving gradient stability during training and distillation.
key_points: Softmax Collapse rounds target logit gradients to zero when one logit dominates, causing gradients to violate the zero-sum property.
Softmax Cancellation produces false non-zero gradients when student and teacher logits match during distillation.
The proposed fix eliminates the Slingshot phenomenon, accelerates grokking with weight decay, and prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay.
Bound logit growth post-memorization is established via an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's epsilon hyperparameter.
summary.why_it_matters: Fixing these fundamental numerical instabilities prevents model drift during knowledge distillation and stabilizes long-term neural network training dynamics.

papers.title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: TWICE introduces twin-world credit assignment for agentic RL by re-using Gumbel noise across counterfactual rollouts to reduce advantage estimation variance.
key_points: Identifies that deterministic elements in agentic search (retriever, corpus, grader) make twin worlds realizable by keying Gumbel sampling noise by turn and line.
Derives an unbiased turn-level advantage estimator whose variance scales by 1-ρ (where ρ is outcome correlation), reducing required rollouts to resolve advantage Δ from Θ(Δ⁻²) to Θ(Δ⁻¹).
Uses a square-root budget allocation rule to spend twin rollouts where outcomes are predicted to disagree per unit computational cost.
Improves GRPO average exact match by 5.3 points on Qwen2.5-3B and 4.5 points on Qwen2.5-7B across seven QA benchmarks while using 68% fewer auxiliary tokens than VinePPO.
summary.why_it_matters: By isolating decision impact from downstream stochastic luck, TWICE significantly improves agentic RL performance while cutting the auxiliary compute costs of counterfactual credit assignment.

papers.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems

summary.tldr: IQuest-Q1 is an open-source 320B sparse Mixture-of-Experts agentic foundation model (15B active) trained via a three-stage pipeline and model merging to enhance coding and general agentic CLI capabilities.
key_points: Architecture: 320B total parameters with 15B activated per token using a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design.

Pre-training & Mid-training: Combines Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum that increases coding data, followed by fine-grained mid-training for domain expansion and context extension.
Post-training & Merging: Employs multi-scaffold post-training (SFT, domain-specialized RL, and MOPD) and merges checkpoints and experts across training stages to resolve parameter update conflicts.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides the open-source community with a large-scale, highly activated-efficient MoE model optimized specifically for complex CLI and coding agent workflows.

papers.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence

summary.tldr: EpiSEM-Bench is an executable benchmark evaluating how ten tool-using LLM agents handle unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery when critical facts are omitted from environment responses.
key_points: Evaluates agent safety using 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six distinct domains.
Systematically suppresses critical facts to measure unsafe execution rates under evidence omission and determine minimum observed failure cardinality.
Features an independent audit tool to verify if agents proactively search for missing facts and appropriately withhold prohibited actions while completing allowed tasks.

Demonstrates that while providing recovery access reduces unsafe execution across all ten evaluated models, resistance to missing evidence does not guarantee successful evidence recovery or appropriate action.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes a critical vulnerability where tool-using LLMs execute unsafe actions due to true but incomplete environmental responses, providing a standardized framework to measure and improve agent robustness.

papers.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3

summary.tldr: Evaluating OLMo-3 checkpoints with InstrumentalEval reveals that RLVR causes a nonmonotonic trajectory in instrumental behavior, initially rising before dropping below the SFT baseline at final checkpoints.
key_points: Evaluations of OLMo-3-7B-Think show instrumental behavior rates move nonmonotonically from 25.0% at SFT, peaking at 46.1% near RLVR step 200, and declining to 11.8% at the final RLVR checkpoint.
Preliminary tests on a 32B model variant show a similar overall reduction, dropping from a 35.53% rate at SFT to 22.37% at the final RLVR step.

Prompt framing accounts for only 15% of average within-checkpoint score variance, and removing detectable framing directions via Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) does not alter the overall SFT-to-final-RLVR reduction.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings challenge the assumption that reinforcement learning monotonically increases dangerous instrumental-convergence subgoals in language models over the course of training.

papers.title: Simulated Control Evals

summary.tldr: Simulated control evaluations (SCEs) use a language model to simulate tool responses, providing more accurate safety predictions for AI deployments than separate executed control settings.
key_points: SCEs use an LLM to simulate tool environments and were benchmarked against execution ground-truth on LinuxArena and a separate setting, BashArena.
Across five monitors at a 5% audit budget, SCEs predicted safety with a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 3.6 percentage points, compared to 10.1 for BashArena.
SCEs reduced KL divergence for attack strategies and reasoning by over 10-fold compared to BashArena and explained 78-85% of between-environment variance.
Sample efficiency is high, requiring under 5% as many task-pair draws as the deployment task set to outperform BashArena in safety prediction accuracy.
Attack strategies discovered in simulation improved monitor performance on held-out attacks, matching the improvement gained from executed strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: SCEs allow cheap, deployment-specific safety and control evaluations without building complex execution environments, outperforming standard off-environment control benchmarks.

papers.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers used mechanistic interpretability to discover causal subspaces for metaphor in LLMs, enabling direct steering of metaphoricity in both classification and generation tasks.
key_points: Identified causal subspaces representing metaphor across multiple LLM architectures and model sizes.
Demonstrated successful steering of LLM classification outputs across various parts of speech using mechanistic interpretability techniques.
Validated representation steering on text generation tasks to actively control the metaphoricity of generated outputs.
summary.why_it_matters: Mapping and manipulating metaphor-specific subspaces allows researchers to directly control abstract cognitive and stylistic properties in LLM generations.

papers.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection

summary.tldr: A small Qwen3-8B model post-trained with reinforcement learning achieves transferable tool selection across different retrievers and unseen tool corpora, outperforming the much larger Llama-4-Maverick (402B) on ToolBench.
key_points: Uses reinforcement learning to train a small open language model to decompose instructions and select tools from retrieved candidates.
A post-trained Qwen3-8B model surpasses the 402B-parameter Llama-4-Maverick on the ToolBench benchmark.
The trained model transfers directly to alternative retrievers and generalizes to unseen tool corpora in new domains without retriever-specific retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: This demonstrates that small open-weights models trained with RL can replace massive proprietary LLMs for multi-step tool selection across scale-constrained tool environments.

papers.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery

summary.tldr: A new coding agent framework introduces Adaptive Skill Granularity, combining a feature-based granularity controller with a finite-state recovery executor to dynamically shift between macro skills and micro-level tool recovery.
key_points: Treats skill granularity as an action-abstraction policy conditioned on task structure, execution state, and macro-skill failures.
Combines a feature-based granularity controller for runtime routing with a finite-state recovery executor for macro-to-micro transitions.
Addresses the brittleness of fixed macro execution by enabling adaptive hybrid execution that recovers from controlled macro failures.
Evaluated on a deterministic coding-agent protocol using verifier-defined success, total cost, and process metrics including macro adoption, route match, and transition correctness.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that agent skill libraries should be managed as controllable, recoverable execution abstractions rather than simple static retrieval resources, improving robustness in code generation.

papers.title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels

summary.tldr: DIAL enables fine-grained numerical control over instruction adherence in LLMs using classifier-free guidance distillation and a text-conditioned, closed-form steering adapter.
key_points: Uses frozen LLM classifier-free guidance (CFG) to provide training signals for on-policy distillation of instruction adherence at varying levels.
Employs a lightweight, text-conditioned steering adapter that uses a hidden-state classifier to compute a closed-form edit, adaptively scaling steering magnitude per token to maintain coherence.
Supports broad instruction scalability using a shared adapter trained solely on instruction and request text without per-instruction fitting.
Introduces SteerIF, an instruction-only dataset containing 98,625 concept, persona, verifiable, and descriptive instructions.
Demonstrates monotonic increases in concept scores across adherence levels while improving persona control and verifiable instruction following.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a computationally efficient and scalable method to dynamically dial the intensity of LLM traits and constraint adherence without retraining models per instruction.

papers.title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity

summary.tldr: Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS) formalizes automated agent architecture adaptation under non-stationary shifts as sequential incumbent replacement using risk-constrained graph edits, paired shadow replay, interventional credit assignment, and canary stages.
key_points: CMAS evaluates typed graph edits against an incumbent via paired shadow replay using common random numbers and interventional component credit.
Promotion requires a variance-penalized score above a set margin, followed by a simulated canary stage with pre-specified rollback mechanisms.
Evaluated on MetaInvest-Bench across 96 streams, CMAS reduced normalized surrogate dynamic-oracle regret from 0.116 to 0.104 and increased held-out utility from 0.44 to 0.48.
CMAS achieved a 3.4% per-update false-promotion rate against a 5% nominal target (4.8% in a sealed rerun) and lowered deployment inference cost by ~6%.
Search-inclusive token costs are higher, and the method's empirical calibration does not guarantee sequence-level error control or complete absence of canary-stage harm.
summary.why_it_matters: CMAS provides a safer, risk-bounded approach to automatically reconfiguring multi-agent graph architectures in production environments without requiring manual re-engineering during distribution shifts.

papers.title: Predictable performance is suboptimal, and what it means for model routing

summary.tldr: A study shows performance predictors only outperform a model's self-confidence when the model is suboptimal or the predictor adds significant parameter capacity, with advantages diminishing as models undergo finetuning.
key_points: Performance predictor advantages over a model's self-confidence transfer exactly in log loss through recalibration.
The theoretical advantage of a predictor is bounded by the candidate model's suboptimality plus the capacity gain from the predictor's extra parameters.
Experiments across 16 language models on four benchmarks confirm that predictor-based routing outperforms self-confidence-based cascading mostly on suboptimal models.
Finetuning candidate models improves their baseline reliability, shrinking the relative advantage of external performance predictors in two-model cascades.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that training external routing predictors offers limited benefit over simple model self-confidence unless the base model is uncalibrated, suboptimal, or augmented with significant extra parameter capacity.

papers.title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers show that multilingual LLMs fail at cross-script entity matching due to miscalibrated decision criteria rather than lost representation, and locate a middle-layer causal intervention site that restores performance.
key_points: Qwen2.5-7B same-person accuracy drops from 35.1% in Latin to 8.5% in Devanagari (Marathi prompts) and 5.3% in Malayalam, while different-person accuracy remains above 98%.
Latin-trained probes successfully extract identity labels from Devanagari hidden states, and scalar calibration recovers 87% of the model-probe balanced-accuracy gap.
Activation patching isolates causal sensitivity to the second entity in Qwen's middle layers, where a single shared sensitivity direction transfers half the full-state margin correction.
A fact-independent intervention at this middle-layer site increases held-out Marathi same-person accuracy from 6.5% to 33.5% while retaining 98.5% different-person accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: Cross-script entity matching failures in LLMs can be mitigated by adjusting internal decision thresholds without retraining or providing additional factual knowledge.

papers.title: HERD: Harness-Evolving Recursive Distillation for Continual Learning

summary.tldr: HERD is a hybrid continual learning framework that combines evolving in-context harness skills with drift-constrained recursive distillation into parameters to minimize catastrophic forgetting.
key_points: Harness side continuously refines reusable skills and retains high-residual failure examples in bounded memory.
Parameter side uses drift-constrained distillation with dual anchors to prevent forgetting across long recursive iterations.
Evaluated on a 25-stage TRACE+17 task stream under fixed memory and compute constraints.
Matches top parametric baselines in acquiring new tasks while showing lower forgetting and superior retention of general capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: HERD provides a scalable architecture for lifetime model updating by bridging context-based in-context learning with stable parametric model updates under strict compute budgets.

papers.title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: ValuSpec is a plug-and-play candidate valuation mechanism that filters low-quality branches from candidate trees prior to target-side verification in tree-based speculative decoding.
key_points: Uses transfer-based supervision to align tree filtering directly with the target model's behavior.
Estimates filtering thresholds from the target model's greedy trajectories using a calibration split without parameter training.
Guarantees output identity to standard autoregressive decoding by verifying the pruned tree under the target model's output-identical greedy rule.
Achieves up to 2.38x end-to-end speedup in retrieval-based tree settings and up to 2.78x speedup when integrated into EAGLE-3.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves LLM inference efficiency by preventing wasteful target-side computation on low-quality tree branches without requiring model retraining or altering decoding accuracy.

papers.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

summary.tldr: Researchers identify State Integrity Collapse, a phenomenon in long-horizon dialogues where LLMs recall stated instructions but fail to execute them, and introduce the StateTrack-Bench evaluation suite.
key_points: State Integrity Collapse is defined as recall-compliance dissociation where models preserve constraints in memory yet fail to apply them in later turns.
StateTrack-Bench tests conversations up to 50 turns across numerical, format, persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints.
A forked recall audit reveals that 88.6% of failures (84.4% excluding a brittle outlier model) stem from behavioral drift rather than forgetting.
Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 accuracy points on immutable constraints during extended dialogues.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-turn instruction-following evaluations are insufficient to guarantee LLM reliability, as models frequently stop applying remembered constraints as dialogue state grows.

papers.title: Memory-Aware Reward Modeling: Learning Human Preferences for LLM Memory Use

summary.tldr: Researchers collected ~1,000 pairwise human judgments to evaluate LLM memory use, revealing that users often prefer memory-free responses and that a new memory-aware reward model outperforms baseline evaluators with 72.8% preference prediction accuracy.
key_points: Empirical study evaluated memory use via ~1,000 pairwise judgments from 87 participants using their real ChatGPT queries and personal memories.
Users do not consistently prefer memory-conditioned responses over non-memory responses, strongly preferring memory-free outputs in certain cases.
Automatic evaluators show low agreement with human preferences, demonstrating a systemic bias that favors memory-conditioned responses significantly more than users do.
A novel memory-aware reward model trained on human judgments achieves 72.8% preference prediction accuracy, outperforming existing baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Current memory mechanisms and automated benchmarks over-prioritize memory injection, highlighting the need for memory-aware reward models to align retention and context use with actual user preferences.

papers.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing

summary.tldr: SpectralCanary is a proactive text-to-image dataset-use auditing method that blends a low-frequency canary image into training data using a smooth low-pass mask without requiring auxiliary models or per-image optimization.
key_points: Uses a smooth low-pass mask to embed a fixed canary image into dataset images while leaving text captions untouched.
Achieves a 91.1% average per-generation TPR at 1% FPR and 94.8% model-level accuracy with 30 generations on the Pokemon dataset across two architecture families.
Maintains high image fidelity across five diverse domain datasets using SD3.5, recording an SSIM of 0.989, LPIPS of 0.022, and a mean ΔFID of 0.05.
Ablation studies confirm low-frequency signal placement transfers to model outputs more reliably than mid- or high-frequency placements.
Resists adaptive removal attacks, which require aggressive image modifications exceeding 25 ΔFID points to successfully erase the signal.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables model owners and creators to reliably audit whether proprietary image collections were used to fine-tune text-to-image models with minimal impact on image quality.

papers.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing

summary.tldr: BeNice! is a two-stage method combining pretraining stochastic depth with post-training KV-cache broadcasting to enable depth-wise KV-sharing in looped language architectures without losing model quality.
key_points: Uses stochastic depth during pretraining to induce contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across loop recurrences.
Applies BeNice! post-training to broadcast the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals.
Matches standard finetuning unshared validation perplexity while eliminating the linear KV-cache memory growth of looped models.
Composes with low-precision quantization (FP8, MXFP8, NVFP4) and efficient sequence mixers like Multi-Latent Attention and Kimi Delta Attention.
Improves simulated low-memory long-context performance, raising cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, boosting throughput by up to 23.6%, and reducing p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the linear KV-cache memory overhead inherent to looped parameter-efficient architectures, significantly reducing latency and memory usage during long-context inference.

security.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders

summary.tldr: End-to-end gradient attacks on neural receivers fail due to gradient masking from unrolled LDPC decoder saturation, but new losses bypassing or supervising early iterations restore attack efficacy.
key_points: Identified gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the belief-propagation check-node boxplus operation, decaying gradient norms by over four orders of magnitude across 10 unrolled iterations.
Proposed L_BP, which applies per-iteration supervision to route gradients through unsaturated early iterations of the unrolled LDPC decoder.
Proposed L_LLR, a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios that completely bypasses the decoder's computational graph.
Demonstrated that both loss functions increase block-error rate (BLER) by 1 to 4 orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power across Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx architectures.
Observed that L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to 3 orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations compared to L_BP at low perturbation-to-signal ratios (PSR).
summary.why_it_matters: The findings reveal critical security vulnerabilities in end-to-end 5G NR neural receivers, demonstrating that safety from gradient attacks was an artifact of gradient masking rather than actual physical robustness.

security.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift

summary.tldr: VX-One is a small, multi-task decision network (100K-10M parameters) that delivers typed, calibrated outputs for real-time perimeter triage in ~0.7-1.7 ms p50 CPU latency.
key_points: Achieves sub-2ms CPU p50 latency and outperforms baselines in binary detection under temporal drift on CIC-IDS2017 (AUROC 0.711 vs 0.637), though XGBoost still wins on multi-class attribution.
Tested as a Phase 2 model following Suricata (52,674 rules), resolving the ~99.9% gray-zone traffic left by signatures on payload-less flows to achieve combined recall >=0.978.

Exhibits limitations under unseen attack families and drift: abstention thresholds transfer poorly across datasets, and calibration collapses under temporal drift across all evaluated models (ECE rises from 0.04 to 0.40).
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that lightweight, typed multi-task networks can efficiently resolve signature-engine gray zones at the network edge, while highlighting critical calibration failures under temporal drift.

security.title: Parameters efficient language model with latent cross-attention for IoT intrusion detection

summary.tldr: A compact Transformer architecture uses latent cross-attention compression to achieve high-accuracy IoT intrusion detection with only 306k non-embedding parameters.
key_points: Compresses input into a small latent space prior to processing with a minimal Transformer core, totaling 1.6M parameters (6MB) and 306k non-embedding parameters.
Outperforms SecurityBERT by ~2 points in macro F1-score on Edge-IIoTset and performs within 0.7 points on CICIoT2023, while being 7x smaller and ~89x faster on simulated edge hardware.
Demonstrates that a single Transformer layer is sufficient and that parameter sharing matches layer stacking performance while reducing parameters by up to 66%.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that Transformer-based intrusion detection can be deployed efficiently on memory-constrained IoT edge devices without sacrificing classification accuracy.

infra.title: Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at Scale: vLLM Matches DeepInfer and Scales to GB300 NVL72

summary.tldr: vLLM scales DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serving to a full GB300 NVL72 rack using P/D disaggregation and Wide-EP, matching DeepSeek's native DeepInfer engine throughput within 6%.
key_points: Achieves 954K tokens/s per GPU at a P90 latency of 196 tokens/s per user on the SemiAnalysis AgentX benchmark using GB300 NVL72.
Delivers a 7.9x throughput increase over single-node aggregated results and reaches 826 tokens/s for a single user via a specialized low-latency decode path.
Matches DeepInfer's decode throughput within 6% across batch sizes 8–256 at 131K context with nextn=3.
Integrates open-source DeepSeek kernels including MegaAttn, MegaMoE, and Mega-mHC, utilizing DEP2 prefill without redundant experts.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that general-purpose open-source serving frameworks like vLLM can match specialized, vendor-native inference engines at rack-scale deployment.

infra.title: Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine

summary.tldr: AWS has upgraded the Amazon Polly Generative engine, adding 14 new voices across 9 locales, introducing Hindi and Finnish, and expanding Region availability to AWS GovCloud (US-West).
key_points: Drop-in upgrade for existing generative voices that requires no changes to API calls or voice names.
Brings the total generative voice catalog to 57 voices across 11 languages and 25 locales.
Adds 14 new voices including US English (Kenneth, Nate), Australian English (Russell, Curtis), Hindi (Kiara, Arjun), and Finnish (Suvi).
Offers context-based speech delivery that adapts emotion, prosody, and accuracy for numbers, currency, and addresses without manual setup.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can automatically access improved speech accuracy, expressive prosody, and broader language support without rewriting existing AWS API integrations or IAM policies.

summary.tldr: OpenAI published an index page defining the role of Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) within the organization.
key_points: OpenAI outlines its internal definition and functional scope for Forward Deployed Engineering.
The role focuses on bridging technical deployment with direct application requirements.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding OpenAI's internal roles provides clarity on how the organization structures its technical integration and customer-facing deployment teams.

vendors.title: Uber brings ChatGPT Work to all employees with OpenAI

summary.tldr: Uber is deploying ChatGPT Work to over 30,000 employees across the enterprise.
key_points: ChatGPT Work deployment covers more than 30,000 Uber employees.
Employees will use the platform for research, data analysis, presentation creation, and executing complex workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: This enterprise-wide deployment integrates generative AI directly into routine operational workflows for thousands of Uber employees.

vendors.title: How AT&T is rethinking in-house legal work with OpenAI

summary.tldr: AT&T's LegalEdge team is collaborating with OpenAI to streamline legal intake and improve access to internal legal knowledge.
key_points: AT&T is utilizing OpenAI technology to simplify access to legal knowledge.
The LegalEdge team is redesigning legal intake processes to better scale legal judgment across the organization.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating OpenAI models into internal workflows allows corporate legal teams to scale their expertise and resolve legal requests more efficiently.

vendors.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform

summary.tldr: OpenAI has expanded ChatGPT Ads to 26 new countries, following adoption by over 100,000 advertisers.
key_points: ChatGPT Ads access expanded to 26 additional countries.
Platform adoption reached over 100,000 advertisers ranging from local businesses to global brands.
Ad placements target users while they explore, compare, and make purchasing decisions within ChatGPT.
summary.why_it_matters: The geographic expansion and advertiser growth scale OpenAI's ability to monetize ChatGPT user intent during product discovery and purchasing decisions.
